data.name: Revulsion
data.detailed_description:
Revulsion takes classic Doom and Quake style gameplay and combines it with a loot based shooter. This involves getting better and better weapons and armor as you climb toward the level cap. In addition to that, there is a large amount of potential loot that you can discover to help you along the way. Weapons, armor, and even special abilities that are tied to limited resources. You will have the ability to craft items from blueprints, as well as repairing broken items that you may find throughout the world. You will navigate both hand crafted and randomly generated level design to unravel a series of increasingly more dangerous environments.

Revulsion is a game that is meant to challenge you without being unfair.

Hello, I am TheCastle, and the sole developer on this project. You have very likely played other games I have worked on at some point in the past. I often release Revulsion updates and I do my best to listen to feedback. If you like the work you see here, then please consider supporting me by buying the game!

reviews.review:
[h1] In A Nutshell [/h1]

🔵 [b] Pros [/b]
+ Well made, engaging mix between Old School FPS and Action RPG genres. 
+ Challenging, fast and lethal combat requiring skill, but also knowledge in approaching enemies with the right equip.
+ Satisfying gun-play, with weapons being well diversified from each other, and generally well balanced.
+ Decently deep item crafting / upgrading mechanics, with new blueprints, gear to acquire and unlock progressively.
+ The constant risk of losing every gear piece and credits because of death adds even more challenge, in a dark souls fashion.

🔴 [b] Cons [/b]
- Lack of a character attribute system or skill trees, limiting the Action RPG progression aspects to loot and gear only. 
- After clearing all the hand-crafted content (around 6-8 hours), players have to replay already cleared levels again, exactly the same as before, only with up-scaled enemy ranks.

If I had to describe Revulsion to someone, i'd probably say it's a mix between Borderlands and Quake 2. On one side, there is a solid ARPG gear and crafting system in place, featuring color-coded loot of several qualities, crafting materials to acquire, and a lot of statistics to compare to determine what the most effective character build is. On the other, nostalgics will feel at home with low-poly, retro styled Classic FPS mechanics, reminding a lot of games such as Quake 2 or DOOM, both in style and gameplay, where high-speed strafing, mobility on the field and dodging heaps of bullets are the norm. 

One of the first good points to mention is definitely weapons feel, with each weapon having a very distinct handling to it, and also a very precise role on the battlefield: automatic shotguns are great for dealing with crowds of weaker enemies, as are flamethrowers, but for tougher single enemies maybe a railgun or rocket launcher would be preferable, always depending on the enemy's weaknesses to one of the several damage types. Killing enemies also holds its satisfaction, with ragdoll physics and dismemberment often resulting into piles of bloody chunks and corpses flying all over.

A good mention should be made for the ARPG loot system, opening up to a variety of play-styles, it's just a shame also a character progression system and skill trees were not included, to deepen even more the class building experience. 

On the bad side, I have to say the overall style, even if reminiscent of old school games, feels a bit anonymous and without a definite style to it, but rather a mashup of different settings put together. The fact all stages after Level 25, or at least all of which i've seen so far nearing level 40, are recycled from the already seen stages, is something that disappoints.

[u]Overall, Revulsion is quite a good title, succeeding in delivering the gameplay experience expected from this sub-genre of FPS/RPG mix, with some unique mechanics to it and its own style. Old school fps and ARPG lovers will surely like it, as I certainly did.[/u]

[quote]Liked this review, and want to see more of the same quality? Check out [url=https://store.steampowered.com/curator/39323490]Tamaster's Review Archive[/url] to see all my Reviews in a single, convenient location.[/quote]

[h1] In-depth Feature Analysis [/h1]


🎮 [b] Gameplay [/b]
The gameplay of Revulsion is divided into Exploration, Combat, and Character Management. 

Stage layout in Revulsion is built into a classic FPS fashion, with generally intricate maps featuring many rooms filled with enemies, and a series of objectives to get to in order to unlock the exit and proceed to the next stage. During the main campaign, each stage battery is composed of 2-3 maps, which then becomes 4-5 once reaching Level 25-30 content and replaying them again, as procedural random levels are thrown into the mix. An handy and quite stylish 3D map is always available to keep track of objective, ammo, and collectible locations, but not enemies. Fast travel platforms are present in each level in many places, and act as Dark Souls' bonfires, allowing players to rest and eventually return to the Sanctuary, their base, to craft new weapons, put stuff into the storage, and generally sort out inventories and newfound gear. This though, will make all killed enemies also re-spawn!

Character Management is quite deep in Revulsion, featuring slots for various body parts' armor, one for an healing item, a Special tool, and seven different lot for weapons, each with a specific arms category. Each piece of armor, depending on eventual upgrades and quality, will give different bonuses and even maluses, like greater armor for reduced movement speed. Weapons do not give passive bonuses, but instead feature different damage types, each specifically effective against certain types of enemies. 
At Sanctuary, players are able to store, scrap, upgrade and craft from scratch all types of gear, tools and weapons, using the crafting materials found in levels from loot, enemies. Keeping up with the current stage level and be "on par" with your gear levels is fundamental.

📖 [b] Story [/b]
N/A

👊 [b] Combat System [/b]
Combat in this title is fast paced and complex at the same time. Players will need to become adept at dodging bullets strafing all over the place as in any old school shooter, and at the same time calculate weaknesses and resistances of enemies based on their current gear, something that is crucial later on when enemies become lethal and very tough. It pays out to have varied damage types in the weapon load-out. 

Health and Armor are the main stats one needs to take care of, but also Action Points are a thing, needed to use special tools and acting as "mana", to activate Healing and Special tools, present in various forms with greatly different effects, from buffs, healing AoE, bullet-stopping walls, to time slowing.


💰 [b] Content & Pricing [/b]
Priced at 15€, the game offers a very variable amount of content depending on how much a player is inclined to repeat already passed levels for the sake of grinding and becoming more and more powerful, until reaching Level 100 and the final boss. The hand-crafted content lasts until level 25-30 and is about 6-8 hours, after that random gen levels and repeated maps come into play, and not all may like that. Still, for this price, the game offers good quality content and lots of fun, so it's worth the price.

🔗 [b] Balance & Challenge [/b]
Generally, enemies and weapons are well balanced, offering a good degree of challenge but also never being overpowered on either side (enemy or player's). As the game progresses, expect challenge to ramp up considerably. I liked how this game managed to equalize loot stats and player skill not making any of the two predominant.


[h1] Technical Analysis [/h1]


🎥 [b] Graphics [/b]
Low poly graphics that suit well the old school gameplay style. Some modern effects like physics are thrown into the mix. Generally pleasant but not really amazing to look at. 

🔊 [b] Sound [/b]
Average sounds and quite good soundtrack especially during battles and horde spawns.

🔩 [b] Performance & Stability [/b]
Good overall, fps problems in procedural levels were fixed in a recent patch. [i7 4820K, GTX1080, 16GB RAM]

💻 [b] Artificial Intelligence [/b]
Enemies as expected just follow and attack the player. Typical in this game genre.

🏠 [b] Quality of Life [/b]
Functional interfaces and menus, but the game could use a more detailed tutorial on crafting and several mechanics. 

🐛 [b] Bugs & Issues [/b]
Nothing major to report.


[h1] Conclusion [/h1]
Revulsion is definitely a successful mix of FPS and ARPG, targeted to hardcore, old-school players mostly, and featuring a level of challenge not everyone is used to nowadays. Still, FPS veterans and RPG lovers will find plenty of fun in it.

This product was reviewed using a free key provided by the Developers.
